newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israelis appeal to court to charge Netanyahu.
newsitem.headline: Israelis appeal to court to charge Netanyahu.

text.p: Israeli opposition members and a public watchdog group served three appeals to the High Court of Justice on Monday demanding an indictment against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in a corruption scandal, a court spokesman said.
The appellants told the court a decision by prosecutors not to press charges for lack of evidence, announced on Sunday, was "highly unreasonable," leftist legislator Yossi Sarid told army radio.
"Three appeals have been served to the court but there will be no discussion of the appeals today," court spokesman Moshe Gorali told Reuters.

State Attorney Edna Arbel told a news conference on Sunday some of her prosecution colleagues had wanted to indict Netanyahu and Justice Minister Tzachi Hanegbi over the short-lived appointment of an attorney general in January.
But in the end presocutors said only Netanyahu's political ally Aryeh Deri, already facing corruption charges, should be indicted and a Netanyahu aide will face further investigation.

Legal analysts said the appeals by Sarid, Labour members Yossi Beilin and Yonah Yahav, and the Movement for Quality Government, had little chance of succeeding in forcing the prosecution to press charges.
